saints.name: St. Matilda
saints.title: Queen
saints.shortBlurb: The devout queen of Germany, wife of Henry the Fowler and mother of Otto the Great, known for her almsgiving…
biography: Born about 895 at Engern in Westphalia and brought up at the monastery of Erfurt, Matilda married in 909 Henry, duke of Saxony, afterward King Henry I of Germany, called the Fowler. She bore him five children, among them the emperor Otto I, Henry duke of Bavaria, and Bruno, later archbishop of Cologne.

Widowed in 936, she favored the claim of her son Henry to the crown against his brother Otto, and in later years both sons turned on her, charging that her lavish alms had impoverished the crown. She surrendered her dower lands and withdrew to her villa at Engern, yet was reconciled to her sons when misfortune overtook them.

Her chief monastic foundations were Quedlinburg, Nordhausen, Engern, and Pöhlde. She died at the convent of Quedlinburg on 14 March 968 and was buried beside her husband, venerated as a saint immediately after her death. A queen of unstinting charity and a long-widowed mother of kings, she is honoured as a patron of queens and of widows.
saints.knownFor: Her charity, monastic foundations, and patience amid family strife.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 14 March
